image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a green tiger beetle resting on dry, brown leaf litter and soil. The beetle has a vibrant metallic green exoskeleton with distinct pale/white spots on its elytra. Its head is visible with large compound eyes and long antennae. Six legs are present, gripping the ground. The background consists of out-of-focus organic debris.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head broader than pronotum with large prominent compound eyes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, appearing wider than the neck/pronotum area, and features large, bulging compound eyes characteristic of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long sickle-shaped mandibles adapted for capturing prey.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Prominent, elongated mandibles are visible extending from the front of the head, consistent with the 'sickle-shaped' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Filiform antennae extending well beyond the midbody.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Long, thread-like antennae are visible extending backwards along the body, surpassing the midpoint of the elytra.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated, slender body with distinctly narrow proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall body shape is oval but relatively slender and elongated, fitting the description of an active predatory beetle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bright metallic coloration in green, bronze, or copper tones.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The elytra exhibit a strong, iridescent metallic green sheen, matching the taxonomy prior perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive pale markings on smooth iridescent elytra.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Several irregular white/cream-colored spots are clearly visible on the green wing covers (elytra).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Six slender cursorial legs enabling rapid pursuit.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Three legs are visible on the left side and three on the right side (though some are partially obscured by angle/shadow), totaling six. They appear slender and jointed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (head, thorax, abdomen).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture appears hard and shiny (chitinous). The segmentation between head, thorax, and elytra-covered abdomen is visually distinct.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification of species identity and fine-grained taxonomic features (metallic sheen, spot pattern).
To ensure thin structures like legs and antennae do not merge with the complex background or show fusion artifacts.
To check for subtle texture anomalies in the metallic reflection or background blur consistency.
To verify the beetle sits correctly on the ground plane without floating or shadow inconsistencies.

focus_areas: Integrity of thin appendages (antennae/legs) against cluttered background
Consistency of metallic reflection and iridescence
Anatomical correctness of mandible attachment and symmetry
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the connection points of the legs to the thorax; AI often fuses these joints. Verify that the white spots on the elytra follow the curvature of the body and do not look like flat overlays. Check if the shadow cast by the beetle matches the lighting direction implied by the highlights on the metallic shell.
